title: Is intrauterine exposure to acetaminophen associated with emotional and hyperactivity problems during childhood? Findings from the 2004 Pelotas birth cohort.
ehr_evidence: We performed a prospective longitudinal population-based study using data from the 2004 Pelotas birth cohort.
summary: Prospective longitudinal birth cohort study investigating the association between prenatal acetaminophen exposure and childhood emotional and hyperactivity symptoms at ages 6 and 11 in a Brazilian population, finding sex-specific associations primarily in boys at age 6.
key_findings: At age 6, intrauterine acetaminophen exposure increased odds of emotional problems in boys (OR = 1.47; 95% CI: 1.07–2.02) and hyperactivity/inattention problems (OR = 1.42; 95% CI: 1.06–1.92).
At age 11, associations for boys were attenuated and lost statistical significance after adjustment (emotional: OR = 1.31; 95% CI: 0.99–1.73; hyperactivity/inattention: OR = 1.25; 95% CI: 0.95–1.65).
No significant associations were observed for girls at either age 6 or 11.
Sensitivity analyses confirmed the effect was specific to acetaminophen, as other nonsteroidal analgesics showed no association with behavioral outcomes.
captured_features: Maternal self-reported acetaminophen use during pregnancy
population: children from the 2004 Pelotas birth cohort in Brazil, assessed at ages 6 and 11 years
limitations: Retrospective recall of maternal medication use may lead to underreporting.
Lack of data on exposure timing (trimester) and dosage.
Potential residual confounding by socioeconomic position.
Absence of information on reasons for medication use (e.g., fever or infection).
